title: Define Data Classification and Retention Standards Across All Systems
narrative: FEDC handles a broad range of data — customer personal data, operational telemetry, financial records, and safety-critical network data — each subject to different regulatory retention and handling requirements. There is currently no consistent framework for classifying data assets or enforcing retention policies. This creates regulatory risk (data held beyond retention limits) and security risk (sensitive data not being protected to an appropriate standard). We define a four-tier data classification framework (Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted) and specify minimum retention and disposal requirements for each tier. All data assets must be classified at the point of creation. Classification metadata must be captured in the data catalogue. Automated enforcement of retention policies will be implemented progressively over 18 months.

requirements.title: Classification at creation
requirements.description: All new data assets must be assigned a classification tier (Public, Internal, Confidential, or Restricted) at the point of creation or ingestion. Unclassified assets are not permitted in production systems.

requirements.title: Retention enforcement
requirements.description: Systems storing Confidential or Restricted data must implement automated retention policies that flag data for review or deletion when the defined retention period is exceeded.

requirements.title: Audit trail
requirements.description: Access to Restricted data must generate an immutable audit log entry recording the identity, timestamp, and purpose of each access event.
